hypothesis: The parent’s row-column-K order walks B with a stride of n and performs no parallel work. Tiled i-k-j accumulation makes B and C accesses contiguous in the output-column loop; keeping an 8x128 C tile and 32x128 B panel active should improve locality. Static ownership of disjoint 8-row tiles can use up to eight threads for larger matrices, while serial execution below n=256 avoids parallel overhead on small cases. These are unmeasured expectations, not a speedup claim.
